questions.question: An object is placed at infinity in front of a convex lens. The image formed is:

options.text: at the focal point, highly diminished (point-sized)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**at the focal point, highly diminished (point-sized)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object is placed at **infinity** in front of a **convex lens**, the rays of light coming from the object are **parallel** to the **principal axis**.
 
• After undergoing **refraction** through the lens, these parallel rays **converge** at the **principal focus (F)** on the opposite side of the lens.
 
• The image formed at the **focal point** is **real** and **inverted**. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• The size of the image is **highly diminished**, often described as **point-sized**, because all the light energy is concentrated at a single point.
 
• The **magnification (m)** in this case is **much less than 1** (m 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convex Lens (Converging Lens):** It is a lens that is **thicker at the center** and thinner at the edges. It **converges** a beam of parallel light rays incident on it.
 
• **Image Formation Summary for Convex Lens:**
 
 
• **Object at 2F:** The image is formed **at 2F** on the other side, is of the **same size**, real, and inverted. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Object beyond 2F:** The image is formed **between F and 2F**, is **diminished**, real, and inverted. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Object at F:** The image is formed at **infinity** and is **highly magnified**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Object between F and O:** The image is formed on the **same side** as the object and is **virtual, erect, and magnified**.
 
 
 
• **Lens Formula:** The relationship between **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by the formula **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**.
 
• **Power of a Lens:** It is the reciprocal of the **focal length** in meters (**P = 1/f**). For a **convex lens**, the power is always **positive**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Real Image:** An image that can be obtained on a **screen** is called a **real image**. In a convex lens, real images are always **inverted**.
 
• **Optical Center (O):** The **central point** of the lens through which a ray of light passes **without any deviation**.
 
• **Principal Axis:** An imaginary line passing through the **centers of curvature** of the two surfaces of the lens.
 
• **Applications:** **Convex lenses** are widely used in **spectacles** to correct **Hypermetropia** (long-sightedness), in **cameras**, **microscopes**, **telescopes**, and **magnifying glasses**.
 
• **Sign Convention:** According to the **Cartesian sign convention**, the **focal length** of a **convex lens** is considered **positive**, while that of a **concave lens** is **negative**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following devices works on the principle of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric motor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **electric motor** is an electromechanical device that converts **electrical energy** into **mechanical energy**.
 
• It operates on the fundamental principle of **magnetic effect of electric current**, specifically the **force experienced by a current-carrying conductor** when placed within an external **magnetic field**.
 
• When a current flows through a coil (armature) placed between the poles of a magnet, the magnetic field produced by the current interacts with the external magnetic field, resulting in a **mechanical force** (torque) that causes the coil to rotate.
 
• The direction of this force is governed by **Fleming’s Left-Hand Rule**, which establishes the relationship between the magnetic field, current, and motion.
 
• This principle allows for the continuous rotation of the motor's **shaft**, which can then be used to perform various types of mechanical work. ***Hence, the correct answer is Electric motor.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transformer**:
 
 
• A **transformer** is a static electrical device that transfers electrical energy between two or more circuits through **electromagnetic induction**.
 
• It works on the principle of **Mutual Induction**, where a changing current in the **primary coil** induces a voltage in the **secondary coil**.
 
• It is primarily used to increase (**step-up**) or decrease (**step-down**) **alternating current (AC)** voltages while keeping the frequency constant.
 
 
 
• **Electric Generator**:
 
 
• An **electric generator** is a device that converts **mechanical energy** into **electrical energy**.
 
• It works on the principle of **Electromagnetic Induction**, discovered by **Michael Faraday** in **1831**.
 
• According to **Faraday's Law**, when a conductor moves through a magnetic field, an **induced electromotive force (EMF)** or current is generated. The direction of this induced current is determined by **Fleming’s Right-Hand Rule**.
 
 
 
• **Resistor**:
 
 
• A **resistor** is a passive two-terminal electrical component that implements **electrical resistance** as a circuit element.
 
• It works based on **Ohm's Law**, which states that the current through a conductor is proportional to the voltage across it (**V = IR**).
 
• Its primary function is to **reduce current flow**, adjust signal levels, and terminate transmission lines by dissipating electrical energy as **heat**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fleming’s Left-Hand Rule**:
 
 
• This rule is used to find the direction of the force in **electric motors**.
 
• If we stretch the **thumb**, **forefinger**, and **middle finger** of the left hand mutually perpendicular to each other:
 
 
• The **Forefinger** represents the direction of the **Magnetic Field**.
 
• The **Middle finger** represents the direction of the **Current**.
 
• The **Thumb** represents the direction of the **Force or Motion** acting on the conductor.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Components of a DC Motor**:
 
 
• **Armature Coil**: A large number of turns of insulated copper wire wound over a soft iron core.
 
• **Strong Field Magnet**: Provides a powerful magnetic field (North and South poles).
 
• **Split Ring Commutator**: Consists of two halves of a metallic ring that **reverses the direction of current** every half rotation to maintain a continuous torque.
 
• **Brushes**: Carbon blocks that maintain electrical contact between the rotating commutator and the external **battery**.
 
 

3f:T

questions.question: If the power of an engine is doubled while the time remains constant, the work done will ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Be doubled**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Power** is defined as the rate at which **work** is done or the rate at which energy is transferred over **time**.
 
• The mathematical relationship between **Power (P)**, **Work (W)**, and **Time (t)** is expressed by the formula: **Power = Work / Time** (or **P = W / t**).
 
• From the above formula, **Work Done** can be calculated as the product of **Power** and **Time**: **W = P × t**.
 
• When the **time (t)** is held **constant**, the **Work Done** becomes **directly proportional** to the **Power** of the engine. This means any change in power will result in a proportional change in work.
 
• If the **Power** is **doubled** (increased by a factor of **2**) while the **time** remains the same, the **Work Done** will also be **multiplied by 2**. ***Hence, the work done will be doubled.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Work Done:** In physics, **Work** is said to be done when a **Force** acts upon an object to cause a **displacement**. The **SI unit** of work is the **Joule (J)**, which is equivalent to **1 Newton-meter (N·m)**.
 
• **Power Units:** The **SI unit** of **Power** is the **Watt (W)**, named in honor of **James Watt**, the developer of the steam engine. **1 Watt** is defined as **1 Joule** of work done per **second** (**1 W = 1 J/s**).
 
• **Scalar Nature:** Both **Work** and **Power** are **scalar quantities**, meaning they have magnitude but no specific direction in space.
 
• **Horsepower (hp):** This is a common non-SI unit of **Power** often used in the automotive and engineering industries. **1 Metric Horsepower** is approximately **735.5 Watts**, while **1 Imperial Horsepower** is approximately **746 Watts**.
 
• **Alternative Formula:** **Power** can also be calculated if the **Force (F)** and **Velocity (v)** are known, using the formula **P = F × v** (assuming the force is in the direction of motion).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dimensional Analysis:** The dimensional formula for **Work** is **[ML²T⁻²]**, while the dimensional formula for **Power** is **[ML²T⁻³]**.
 
• **Time Factor:** If **Work** is kept **constant** instead of time, then **Power** and **Time** are **inversely proportional**. For example, a more powerful engine will take **less time** to complete the same amount of work.
 
• **Energy Conversion:** Since **Work** is a form of **Energy** transfer, **Power** can also be viewed as the rate of energy consumption. For instance, a **100-Watt** light bulb consumes **100 Joules** of electrical energy every **second**.

questions.question: What is the primary characteristic that defines organic compounds?

options.text: They are formed only by living organisms.
They are compounds that conduct electricity in their molten state.
They primarily consist of carbon and hydrogen atoms, forming covalent bonds.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They primarily consist of carbon and hydrogen atoms, forming covalent bonds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Organic compounds** are defined as chemical substances that contain **carbon** atoms, usually bonded to **hydrogen**, and often other elements like **oxygen**, **nitrogen**, **sulfur**, and **phosphorus**.
 
• The defining feature of these compounds is the presence of **carbon-hydrogen (C-H) bonds** and the formation of **covalent bonds**, where atoms share electron pairs. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• Contrary to statement 1, not all organic compounds contain **oxygen**; for example, **hydrocarbons** like **methane (CH4)** and **ethane (C2H6)** consist solely of carbon and hydrogen. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Historically, it was believed that organic compounds could only be produced by living organisms (the **Vital Force Theory**), but this was disproven in **1828** when **Friedrich Wöhler** synthesized **urea** from inorganic materials. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Organic compounds generally do not conduct electricity in their molten state because they are **molecular** in nature and lack **free ions**, unlike **ionic compounds**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tetravalency of Carbon**: Carbon has an **atomic number of 6** and **4 valence electrons**, allowing it to form **four covalent bonds** with other atoms. This versatility allows for the creation of vast, complex molecular structures.
 
• **Catenation**: This is the unique ability of **carbon** atoms to form long chains or rings by bonding with other carbon atoms. This property is the reason why millions of organic compounds exist in nature.
 
• **Hydrocarbons**: These are the simplest organic compounds, categorized into **alkanes** (single bonds), **alkenes** (at least one double bond), and **alkynes** (at least one triple bond). They serve as the **parent framework** for more complex organic molecules.
 
• **Functional Groups**: These are specific clusters of atoms within a molecule that determine its chemical reactivity. Common examples include the **hydroxyl group (-OH)** in alcohols, the **carboxyl group (-COOH)** in organic acids, and the **amino group (-NH2)** in amines.
 
• **Isomerism**: Organic chemistry is characterized by **isomers**, which are compounds with the same **molecular formula** but different **structural arrangements**, leading to different physical and chemical properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bonding Nature**: While inorganic compounds often involve **ionic bonding** (transfer of electrons), organic compounds are almost exclusively **covalent**. This results in lower **melting and boiling points** compared to many inorganic salts.
 
• **Combustibility**: Most organic compounds are highly **inflammable** and react with **oxygen** to produce **carbon dioxide** and **water**.
 
• **Solubility**: According to the "like dissolves like" rule, most organic compounds are **insoluble in water** (a polar solvent) but soluble in **organic solvents** like **benzene**, **ether**, or **chloroform**.
 
• **Applications**: Organic compounds are the basis of all **life on Earth** (DNA, proteins, carbohydrates) and are used extensively in industries to produce **plastics**, **medicines**, **fuels**, and **synthetic fibers**.

questions.question: Which of the following reacts with bases to form salt and water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon dioxide** (**CO2**) is a **non-metallic oxide**. Non-metallic oxides are generally **acidic** in nature because they react with **water** to form **acids** or react with **bases** to form **salt** and **water**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Carbon dioxide is correct.***
 
• When **Carbon dioxide** reacts with a **base** like **Calcium hydroxide** [**Ca(OH)2**], also known as **limewater**, it produces **Calcium carbonate** (**CaCO3**), which is a **salt**, and **water** (**H2O**).
 
• **Sodium oxide** (**Na2O**) is a **metallic oxide**. Most metallic oxides are **basic** in nature and react with **acids** to form salt and water, but they do not typically react with bases in this manner. ***Hence, the statement regarding Sodium oxide is incorrect.***
 
• **Hydrogen gas** (**H2**) is a **diatomic molecule**. It does not possess acidic properties that would allow it to react with a **base** to produce salt and water under standard conditions. ***Hence, the statement regarding Hydrogen gas is incorrect.***
 
• **Calcium hydroxide** [**Ca(OH)2**] is a **strong base**. Bases do not react with other bases to undergo **neutralization**; instead, they react with **acids** or **acidic oxides**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Calcium hydroxide is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Oxides**:
 
 
• **Acidic Oxides**: These are oxides of **non-metals** such as **Sulfur dioxide** (**SO2**), **Nitrogen dioxide** (**NO2**), and **Carbon dioxide** (**CO2**). They have a **pH** value less than **7** when dissolved in water.
 
• **Basic Oxides**: These are oxides of **metals** like **Magnesium oxide** (**MgO**) and **Sodium oxide** (**Na2O**). They react with **acids** to form salt and water and usually have a **pH** value greater than **7**.
 
• **Amphoteric Oxides**: These oxides show both **acidic** and **basic** characteristics. Examples include **Aluminum oxide** (**Al2O3**) and **Zinc oxide** (**ZnO**), which can react with both **acids** and **bases**.
 
• **Neutral Oxides**: These oxides do not react with either acids or bases. Examples include **Carbon monoxide** (**CO**), **Nitrous oxide** (**N2O**), and **Nitric oxide** (**NO**).
 
 
 
• **Neutralization Reaction**:
 
 
• This is a chemical reaction in which an **acid** and a **base** react quantitatively with each other.
 
• The general formula is: **Acid + Base → Salt + Water**.
 
• Since **non-metal oxides** act as acids, the reaction **Non-metal oxide + Base → Salt + Water** is also considered a type of **neutralization**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Limewater Test**: The reaction of **CO2** with **Calcium hydroxide** is a standard laboratory test for the presence of **Carbon dioxide**. The formation of **insoluble** **Calcium carbonate** turns the clear solution **milky**.
 
• **Chemical Equations**:
 
 
• Reaction with **Sodium hydroxide**: **CO2 + 2NaOH → Na2CO3 + H2O**. Here, **Sodium carbonate** is the **salt** formed.
 
• Reaction with **Calcium hydroxide**: **CO2 + Ca(OH)2 → CaCO3 + H2O**. Here, **Calcium carbonate** is the **salt** formed.
 
 
 
• **Periodicity**: In the **Periodic Table**, the **acidity** of oxides increases from **left to right** across a **period** as the elements transition from **metals** to **non-metals**.
</ul

questions.question: What happens after fertilisation in a flowering plant?

options.text: The petals and stamens become the seed, and the ovary forms the embryo.
The ovule becomes a fruit, and the ovary forms the seed.
The ovule becomes the seed, and the ovary becomes the fruit.
The entire flower dries up and falls off without forming any new structures.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The ovule becomes the seed, and the ovary becomes the fruit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **flowering plants** (**angiosperms**), **fertilisation** is the process where the **male gamete** (pollen) fuses with the **female gamete** (egg) to form a **zygote**.
 
• Once **fertilisation** is complete, the **zygote** divides multiple times to form an **embryo** within the **ovule**.
 
• The **ovule** develops a tough protective coat and gradually transforms into a **seed**. The **seed** contains the **embryo** and stored food for the future plant. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Simultaneously, the **ovary** undergoes significant growth and ripening to transform into a **fruit**. The wall of the **ovary** becomes the **pericarp** or the fruit wall.
 
• During this developmental phase, other floral parts such as the **sepals**, **petals**, **stamens**, **style**, and **stigma** generally wither and fall off.
 
• While **statement 1** suggests that **petals** and **stamens** become the **seed** and the **ovary** forms the **embryo**, it is biologically inaccurate as the **embryo** forms from the **zygote** inside the **ovule**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2** incorrectly reverses the roles, stating the **ovule** becomes the **fruit** and the **ovary** forms the **seed**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4** claims the entire flower falls off without forming new structures, ignoring the essential transition into **reproductive units** (fruits and seeds). ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Double Fertilisation:**
 
 
• This is a unique phenomenon in **angiosperms** discovered by **S.G. Nawaschin** in **1898**.
 
• It involves two fusions: **Syngamy** (fusion of egg and male gamete to form a **diploid zygote**) and **Triple Fusion** (fusion of the second male gamete with **polar nuclei** to form the **Primary Endosperm Nucleus**).
 
• The **Endosperm** serves as a highly nutritive tissue that provides nourishment to the developing **embryo**.
 
 
 
• **Fruit Classification:**
 
 
• **True Fruits:** These develop solely from the **mature ovary** after **fertilisation**. Examples include **mango** and **blueberry**.
 
• **False Fruits:** These develop from the **ovary** along with other floral parts like the **thalamus** or **receptacle**. Examples include **apple**, **pear**, and **cashew**.
 
• **Parthenocarpic Fruits:** Fruits that develop without **fertilisation** and are typically **seedless**, such as **banana**.
 
 
 
• **Seed Structure and Germination:**
 
 
• The **integuments** (outer layers) of the **ovule** harden to form the **seed coat** (testa and tegmen).
 
• A **seed** remains in a state of **dormancy** (inactivity) until it encounters favorable conditions like **moisture**, **oxygen**, and suitable **temperature** to undergo **germination**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Post-Fertilisation Summary:**
 
 
• **Zygote** → **Embryo**
 
• **Ovule** → **Seed**
 
• **Ovary** → **Fruit**
 
• **Ovary Wall** → **Pericarp**
 
• **Integuments** → **Seed Coat**
 
 
 
• The formation of **fruit** and **seed** is an evolutionary advantage for plants, facilitating **dispersal** by **wind**, **water**, or **animals** and ensuring the **protection** of the next generation.
</ul

questions.question: When {OH}^- ions are added to an acidic solution, the pH:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In chemistry, the **pH level** of a solution is a measure of the molar concentration of **hydrogen ions (H+)** in the solution and as such is a measure of the acidity or basicity of the solution.
 
• When **hydroxide ions (OH-)** are added to an **acidic solution**, they react with the existing **hydrogen ions (H+)** to form **water molecules (H2O)**. This chemical process is known as **neutralization**.
 
• The concentration of **hydrogen ions (H+)** decreases as they are consumed by the **OH- ions**. Since the **pH scale** is calculated as the negative logarithm of the **H+ ion concentration** (pH = -log[H+]), a reduction in **H+ ions** mathematically leads to a higher **pH value**. ***Hence, the statement that the pH increases is correct.***
 
• An **acidic solution** typically has a **pH value** ranging from **0 to 6.9**. As more **OH- ions** are introduced, the solution moves closer to **pH 7.0**, which is the **neutral point** on the scale.
 
• If the addition of **OH- ions** continues beyond the point of **neutralization**, the solution will eventually become **basic (alkaline)**, resulting in a **pH value** greater than **7**. ***Hence, the correct answer is increases.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The pH Scale:**
 
 
• The **pH scale** was introduced by the Danish biochemist **S.P.L. Sorensen** in the year **1909**. It is used to express the acidity or alkalinity of a solution on a scale of **0 to 14**.
 
• A **pH of 7** represents a **neutral solution**, such as **pure water** at **25 degrees Celsius**.
 
• Solutions with a **pH less than 7** are considered **acidic** (e.g., **gastric juice**, **lemon juice**, and **vinegar**), while those with a **pH greater than 7** are **basic or alkaline** (e.g., **baking soda**, **milk of magnesia**, and **ammonia**).
 
 
 
• **Mathematical Relationship:**
 
 
• The relationship between **pH** and **pOH** is defined by the equation **pH + pOH = 14** at a temperature of **25 degrees Celsius**.
 
• The **ionic product of water (Kw)** is a constant value of **1.0 x 10^-14** at standard temperature. This equilibrium ensures that as **OH- concentration** rises, the **H+ concentration** must fall proportionally.
 
 
 
• **Logarithmic Nature:**
 
 
• The **pH scale** is **logarithmic**, meaning each whole **pH value** below **7** is **ten times** more acidic than the next higher value. For example, a solution with **pH 3** is **10 times** more acidic than a solution with **pH 4** and **100 times** more acidic than a solution with **pH 5**.

• **Phenolphthalein** is a common indicator that remains **colorless** in **acidic solutions** but turns **pink** when the solution becomes **basic (around pH 8.2 to 10)**.
 
 
 
• **Common pH Values:**
 
 
• The **pH of human blood** is slightly **basic**, typically maintained within a narrow range of **7.35 to 7.45** for healthy physiological functioning.
 
• **Acid rain** usually has a **pH value** of less than **5.6**, which can cause significant damage to **aquatic ecosystems** and **limestone structures**.
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**, a **strong base**, can have a **pH** as high as **14**, whereas **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)**, a **strong acid**, can have a **pH** as low as **0**.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of uniform circular motion in daily life?

options.text: A person walking in a straight line
A ceiling fan rotating at constant speed
A bus accelerating on a straight road
A ball rolling down an inclined plane

questions.solution:

• **Uniform Circular Motion (UCM)** is defined as the motion of an object traveling at a **constant speed** along a **circular path**. In this motion, while the speed remains the same, the **direction of velocity** changes continuously at every point.
 
• A **ceiling fan rotating at a constant speed** is a perfect example of this. Once the fan reaches its steady state (fixed speed setting), the tips of the blades describe a **circular trajectory** with a **constant magnitude of velocity**. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*

questions.question: An object is dropped from a height. What is its initial velocity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object is **dropped** from a certain **height**, it is implicitly understood that the object starts its motion from a state of **rest**.
 
• In physics and **kinematics**, the **initial velocity** (represented by the symbol **u**) is the velocity of the object at the exact moment the observation of motion begins (at **time t = 0**).
 
• Since the object is simply released and not thrown or pushed with an external force, its **initial velocity** is exactly **0 m/s**. ***Hence, the statement that the initial velocity is 0 m/s is correct.***
 
• The moment the object is released, the **force of gravity** begins to act on it, causing it to accelerate downwards. However, this acceleration changes the velocity over **time**, meaning the speed is only zero at the very first instant.
 
• The value **9.8 m/s** mentioned in the options is often confused with the **acceleration due to gravity**, but that value is measured in **m/s²**, not **m/s**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concept of Free Fall:**
 
 
• An object is said to be in **free fall** when the only force acting upon it is **gravity**. In such cases, **air resistance** is often neglected in basic physics calculations.
 
• During **free fall**, all objects, regardless of their **mass**, accelerate toward the **Earth** at the same rate, which is approximately **9.8 m/s²**.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):**
 
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity** is a constant vector pointing towards the center of the Earth. Its standard value is **9.80665 m/s²**, though it is frequently rounded to **9.8 m/s²** or **10 m/s²** for simplicity in exams.
 
• It is important to distinguish between **velocity** (speed in a direction) and **acceleration** (rate of change of velocity).
 
 
 
• **Equations of Motion:**
 
 
• For an object **dropped** from rest, the **first equation of motion** is **v = u + gt**. Since **u = 0**, the velocity at any time **t** becomes **v = gt**.
 
• The **distance** (height) fallen can be calculated using **h = ut + ½gt²**. With **u = 0**, this simplifies to **h = ½gt²**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dropped vs. Thrown:** If the question stated the object was **thrown downwards**, the **initial velocity** would be a **non-zero value** (u > 0). If it is **thrown upwards**, the **final velocity** at the peak of its trajectory is **0 m/s**.
 
• **Terminal Velocity:** In a real-world scenario with **air resistance**, a falling object eventually reaches a constant speed called **terminal velocity**, where the **drag force** equals the **gravitational force**.
 
• **Frame of Reference:** Usually, the downward direction is considered **negative** in coordinate systems. Thus, while the **magnitude** of the initial velocity is **0 m/s**, the velocity as it falls would be represented with a negative sign (e.g., **-9.8 m/s** after 1 second).
 
• **Location Variation:** The value of **g** varies slightly depending on **latitude** and **altitude**. It is stronger at the **poles** and weaker at the **equator** due to the Earth's **ellipsoid shape** and **rotation**.

9f:T239

questions.question: What is a major disadvantage of connecting an electric bulb and an electric heater in series, based on their required operating current?

options.text: The total voltage would decrease to zero
They need currents of widely different values to operate properly
The total equivalent resistance would be zero
The current through the heater would stop immediately

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They need currents of widely different values to operate properly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **series circuit**, the **electric current** remains the same through all components connected in the loop. This means the **current** (**I**) flowing through the **electric bulb** is identical to the current flowing through the **electric heater**.
 
• An **electric bulb** and an **electric heater** have significantly different **power ratings**. A typical household bulb may consume **40W to 100W**, while a heater typically consumes **1000W to 2000W**.
 
• Because of these different power requirements, they require **currents** of widely different values to function at their rated capacity. For instance, at **220V**, a **100W bulb** requires approximately **0.45 Amperes**, whereas a **2000W heater** requires nearly **9 Amperes**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• In a series connection, if the **current** is high enough to operate the heater, it will instantly burn out the **filament** of the bulb. Conversely, if the current is low enough for the bulb, the heater will not generate any noticeable heat.
 
• The **total voltage** in a series circuit is divided among the components proportional to their **resistance** (**V = V1 + V2**). It does not decrease to zero. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **total equivalent resistance** in a series circuit is the **sum** of individual resistances (**Rs = R1 + R2**). It is never zero unless the components themselves have no resistance. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **current** does not stop immediately unless the circuit is broken (e.g., the bulb blows out); it simply flows at a sub-optimal level for the high-power device. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ohm's Law:** This fundamental principle states that **V = IR**, where **V** is voltage, **I** is current, and **R** is resistance. In series circuits, the high resistance of a bulb limits the **total current** of the entire circuit, making it insufficient for the heater.
 
• **Resistance of Appliances:** Since **P = V²/R**, for a constant voltage, a high-power device like a **heater** has **low resistance**, while a low-power device like a **bulb** has **high resistance**.
 
• **Parallel Circuits:** This is the standard for **domestic wiring**. In a **parallel circuit**, the **voltage** across each appliance is the same (e.g., **220V** in **India**), allowing each device to draw the **current** it needs independently based on its own resistance.
 
• **Power Consumption:** The formula **P = I²R** shows that heat produced depends on the square of the current. In series, the limited current caused by the bulb's high resistance results in negligible power output for the heater.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Single Point of Failure:** One major disadvantage of **series circuits** is that if one component (like the bulb) **fuses** or is switched off, the entire circuit is broken, and all other components (like the heater) stop working.
 
• **Voltage Division:** In a series arrangement, the component with the **highest resistance** (the bulb) takes the **maximum voltage drop**, leaving very little voltage for the heater to operate.
 
• **Practical Application:** Series circuits are rarely used for appliances but are common in **decorative string lights** (fairy lights), where many small bulbs of the same rating are used together.
 
• **Safety:** Connecting high-load appliances in series with low-load ones can lead to **overheating** of wires or **short circuits** if the bulb's holder or filament cannot handle the potential current surge.

questions.question: Which of the following statements describes biological magnification?

options.text: Increase in concentration of harmful substances at higher trophic levels.
Pollutants are completely broken down by decomposers in the ecosystem.
Energy increases as it flows from producers to consumers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increase in concentration of harmful substances at higher trophic levels**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Biological magnification**, also referred to as **biomagnification**, is the process characterized by the progressive **increase in the concentration** of **toxic substances** (such as **heavy metals** or **persistent organic pollutants**) at each successive **trophic level** of a food chain. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• These **harmful substances** are typically **non-biodegradable**, meaning they cannot be broken down by the metabolism of organisms or environmental decomposers. Consequently, they accumulate in the **tissues** of living beings.
 
• The process is not defined by an increase in **biological activities** like metabolic rates or reproduction, but specifically by the **chemical load** per unit of biomass. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Pollutants involved in biomagnification are resistant to being broken down by **decomposers** (like **bacteria** and **fungi**); their persistence in the environment is what allows them to enter the **food web** and accumulate. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• In any **ecosystem**, according to the **10 percent law** of energy transfer, **energy decreases** as it flows from **producers** to **higher consumers**, whereas the concentration of **toxins increases**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Common Pollutants**: The most frequent chemicals associated with this phenomenon include **DDT (Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane)**, **Mercury**, **Arsenic**, **Lead**, and **Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs)**.
 
• **DDT and Wildlife**: A classic example occurred in the **20th century** when **DDT** usage led to the **thinning of eggshells** in predatory birds like **Bald Eagles** and **Peregrine Falcons**, causing their populations to crash until the chemical was banned in **1972** in the **United States**.
 
• **Human Health Risks**: Humans often occupy the **highest trophic level**. Consumption of contaminated fish can lead to **Mercury poisoning**, famously known as **Minamata Disease**, first discovered in **1956** in **Japan**.
 
• **Lipid Solubility**: Most biomagnifying substances are **lipophilic** (fat-soluble). This means they dissolve in **fats** and **oils** within an organism's body, making them difficult to excrete through water-based systems like **urine**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bioaccumulation vs. Biomagnification**: It is important to distinguish these terms. **Bioaccumulation** occurs within a **single organism** over its **lifespan**, while **biomagnification** describes the increase across the **entire food chain**.
 
• **Trophic Level Concentration**: In an **aquatic ecosystem**, the concentration of **DDT** might start at **0.000003 ppm** (parts per million) in **water**, reach **0.04 ppm** in **zooplankton**, **0.5 ppm** in **small fish**, **2 ppm** in **large fish**, and finally **25 ppm** in **fish-eating birds**.
 
• **Global Regulation**: The **Stockholm Convention** on **Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs)**, adopted in **2001**, is an **international environmental treaty** that aims to eliminate or restrict the production and use of substances that undergo **biomagnification**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a molecule of a compound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**H2O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **molecule of a compound** is defined as a substance formed by the **chemical combination** of **two or more different types of elements** in a **fixed proportion** by mass.
 
• **H2O (Water)** is composed of **two hydrogen atoms** and **one oxygen atom**. Since it contains **different elements** chemically bonded together, it is a **molecule of a compound**. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• **N2 (Nitrogen)** consists of **two atoms** of the **same element** (Nitrogen) bonded together. It is classified as a **homoatomic molecule** or a **molecule of an element**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **He (Helium)** is a **noble gas** and exists as a **single atom** (monoatomic). It does not naturally form molecules with other atoms under standard conditions and is considered an **element** in its simplest form. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **O2 (Oxygen)** is a **diatomic molecule** consisting of **two oxygen atoms**. Because the atoms are of the **same element**, it represents a **molecule of an element** rather than a compound. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Elements:** These are **pure substances** that consist of only **one type of atom**. They cannot be broken down into simpler substances by ordinary **chemical reactions**. Examples include **Carbon (C)**, **Iron (Fe)**, and **Gold (Au)**. There are currently **118** recognized elements in the **Periodic Table**.
 
• **Compounds:** A **compound** is a substance where **atoms of different elements** are held together by **chemical bonds** (ionic or covalent). The properties of a **compound** are distinct from the properties of the **individual elements** that compose it. For instance, **Sodium (Na)** is a reactive metal and **Chlorine (Cl)** is a toxic gas, but together they form **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, which is edible **table salt**.
 
• **Molecules:** A **molecule** is the **smallest unit** of a substance that retains the **chemical properties** of that substance. It can be **homoatomic** (like **O3** or **P4**) or **heteroatomic** (like **CO2** or **CH4**).
 
• **Chemical Formula:** This notation represents the **ratio of atoms** in a substance. In **H2O**, the **numerical subscript** 2 indicates there are **two hydrogen atoms** for every **one oxygen atom**.
 
• **Atomicity:** This refers to the **total number of atoms** present in one **molecule** of an **element** or **compound**. For example, **H2O** has an **atomicity of 3** (2 Hydrogen + 1 Oxygen).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Law of Definite Proportions:** Established by **Joseph Proust** in **1799**, this law states that a **chemical compound** always contains its **constituent elements** in a **fixed ratio by mass**, regardless of how the compound was prepared.
 
• **Noble Gases:** Elements like **Helium (He)**, **Neon (Ne)**, and **Argon (Ar)** are **chemically inert** and usually exist as **single atoms**. They are known as **monoatomic elements**.
 
• **Diatomic Elements:** There are **seven elements** that naturally exist as **diatomic molecules** (molecules of two atoms) in their gaseous state: **Hydrogen (H2)**, **Nitrogen (N2)**, **Oxygen (O2)**, **Fluorine (F2)**, **Chlorine (Cl2)**, **Bromine (Br2)**, and **Iodine (I2)**.
 
• **Valency:** The **combining capacity** of an atom is called its **valency**. It determines how many **chemical bonds** an atom can form to create a **molecule** or **compound**. For example, **Oxygen** has a valency of **2**, while **Hydrogen** has a valency of **1**, leading to the formation of **H2O**.
</ul

questions.question: In which part of the female reproductive system does fertilisation take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oviduct (fallopian tube)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fertilisation** is the biological process where a male gamete (**sperm**) fuses with a female gamete (**ovum** or **egg**) to form a **zygote**. In the human female reproductive system, this event specifically occurs in the **Oviduct**, also known as the **Fallopian tube**.
 
• The **fallopian tubes** are a pair of long, narrow ducts that connect the **ovaries** to the **uterus**. They are approximately **10 to 12 cm** in length.
 
• During **ovulation**, a mature egg is released from the **ovary** and is swept into the **fallopian tube** by finger-like projections called **fimbriae**.
 
• Fertilisation usually takes place in the widest section of the fallopian tube, called the **ampulla**. The sperm cells must swim through the **vagina**, **cervix**, and **uterus** to reach the egg in the **oviduct**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the oviduct as the site of fertilisation is correct.***
 
• Once fertilisation occurs, the resulting **zygote** remains in the **fallopian tube** for about **3 to 4 days**, undergoing rapid cell division as it moves toward the **uterus**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ovary**:
 
 
• The **ovaries** are the primary female reproductive organs located on either side of the lower abdomen.
 
• Their main functions are **oogenesis** (the production of eggs) and the secretion of essential hormones like **estrogen** and **progesterone**. Fertilisation does not happen here.
 
 
 
• **Uterus (Womb)**:
 
 
• The **uterus** is a hollow, pear-shaped organ where a fertilised egg implants and develops into a **fetus**.
 
• The process of the embryo attaching to the uterine wall is called **implantation**, which typically occurs about **6 to 9 days** after fertilisation. If fertilisation does not occur, the uterine lining (**endometrium**) is shed during **menstruation**.
 
 
 
• **Cervix**:
 
 
• The **cervix** is the lower, narrow portion of the **uterus** that opens into the **vagina**.
 
• It acts as a gateway that allows **sperm** to enter the uterus and serves as the birth canal during delivery. It also produces **cervical mucus** that changes in consistency throughout the **menstrual cycle** to facilitate or inhibit sperm movement.
 
 
 
• **Zygote to Embryo**:
 
 
• After the **sperm** penetrates the **egg**, the **diploid zygote** is formed. It undergoes **cleavage** (mitotic divisions) to become a **morula** and then a **blastocyst** before reaching the **uterus** for **gestation**.
 
 
</ul

• **Isobars** are atoms of different chemical elements that possess the **same mass number** (A) but have **different atomic numbers** (Z). ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• The **mass number** is the total count of **nucleons**, which includes both **protons** and **neutrons** located in the atomic nucleus.
 
• Because **isobars** have different **atomic numbers**, they represent different chemical elements and occupy different positions in the **Periodic Table**.
 
• A classic example of isobars includes **Argon** (**Ar**), **Potassium** (**K**), and **Calcium** (**Ca**), all of which can have a **mass number** of **40**, while their **atomic numbers** are **18**, **19**, and **20** respectively.
 
• Atoms that share the same **atomic number** but have different **mass numbers** are classified as **isotopes**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Properties like **melting point** and **refractive index** are specific physical and optical characteristics of substances and are not used to define or categorize atomic species such as isobars. ***Hence, options 3 and 4 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Isotopes:**
 
 
• These are variants of a particular chemical element which differ in **neutron number**, and consequently in **nucleon number**.
 
• All **isotopes** of a given element have the same number of **protons** in each atom.
 
• Example: **Hydrogen-1** (Protium), **Hydrogen-2** (Deuterium), and **Hydrogen-3** (Tritium) are the three **isotopes** of hydrogen.
 
 
 
• **Isotones:**
 
 
• These are atoms of different elements that have the same number of **neutrons** but different **atomic numbers** and **mass numbers**.
 
• Example: **Carbon-14** (6 protons, 8 neutrons) and **Oxygen-16** (8 protons, 8 neutrons) are **isotones**.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Isomers:**
 
 
• These are atoms with the same **atomic number** and the same **mass number** but exist in different **energy states** within the nucleus.
 
• They are usually represented by the letter **m** (for metastable) after the mass number, such as **Technetium-99m**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical and Physical Properties:**
 
 
• **Isobars** exhibit completely different **chemical properties** because their electron configurations (determined by the **atomic number**) are different.
 
• Their **physical properties** also differ significantly as they belong to different elements with varying densities and structures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Etymology:** The term **isobar** was first suggested by **Alfred Walter Stewart** in **1918**. It is derived from the Greek words **isos** (equal) and **baros** (weight).
 
• **Beta Decay:** In nuclear physics, **isobars** are frequently produced during **Beta decay**. When a nucleus undergoes **Beta-minus decay**, a **neutron** is converted into a **proton**. This increases the **atomic number** by **1** but the **mass number** remains unchanged, creating an **isobar** of the original element.
 
• **Identification:** **Isobars** can be distinguished using **Mass Spectrometry**, although their mass differences are extremely small (equal to the mass difference between a neutron and a proton-electron pair).
 
• **Stability:** According to **Mattauch's isobar rule**, if two adjacent elements on the **Periodic Table** have isotopes of the same **mass number**, at least one of them must be **radioactive**.
</ul

questions.question: A constant force acts on an object of mass 4 kg for a duration of 2 s. It increases the object’s velocity from 2 m/s to 8 m/s. What is the magnitude of the applied force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• To find the magnitude of the applied force, we use **Newton’s Second Law of Motion**, which states that the force acting on an object is equal to the **mass** of the object multiplied by its **acceleration** (**F = m × a**).
 
• The given parameters in the problem are: **Mass (m) = 4 kg**, **Initial Velocity (u) = 2 m/s**, **Final Velocity (v) = 8 m/s**, and **Time (t) = 2 s**.
 
• First, we must calculate the **acceleration (a)** of the object. Acceleration is defined as the **rate of change of velocity** over time. The formula is **a = (v - u) / t**.
 
• Substituting the values into the acceleration formula: **a = (8 m/s - 2 m/s) / 2 s**. This results in **a = 6 / 2 = 3 m/s²**. Hence, the acceleration of the object is 3
